body:
Concentrated finding round (unified triage seat, 2026-08-17): **promoted to `pm:queue`**, type `Bug`. Real defect with a named mechanism (the recheck state is "has a recheck run", not "which app it ran for") and a low-but-real user cost (a freshly published app reached second in a session shows not-available with no refresh behind it). Fix shape: key `missingRecheck` by the requested app (reset on app-identity change), mirroring how PR #4521 fixed the same shape one state over. S / sonnet–opus.

Container & model: `S`–`M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — triage graded this "S / sonnet–opus". I considered the sonnet floor, since the fix shape is named and its precedent sits in the same file; I went one tier up because the **reproduction test** is the hard part here (a two-consecutive-missing-apps navigation), and a timing test that passes vacuously is the failure mode this card is most likely to produce.
Clause-②: no — internal component state; no contract, no public surface.
Serial constraints cleared: `console/AppContent.tsx` is free; no open PR touches it. Region-disjoint from this round's siblings (#5178 on `views/` + `hooks/`, #5183 on plugin-grid/kanban).

**Parallelism disciplines (app-shell exemption, all four binding):** region declared above; merge `main` before opening the PR; merge again if a sibling lands first; conflicts go to the merge queue.

## Premise re-measured on `origin/main` @ `a2a974779` — holds exactly

```
packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx:233  const [missingRecheck, setMissingRecheck] = useState<'idle'|'checking'|'done'>('idle')
:236  if (missingRecheck !== 'idle') setMissingRecheck('idle')      ← reset ONLY when requestedAppMissing goes false
:239  if (missingRecheck === 'idle' && !metadataLoading && !previewDrafts)
:243  }, [requestedAppMissing, metadataLoading, previewDrafts, missingRecheck, refreshMetadata])
```

The state is a flag about *"a re-check has run"*, not about *which app it ran for* — so missing-app-A → missing-app-B never resets it and the second app gets no re-check.

## Zone 1 — the fix shape is ruled (triage, comment-5320931511)

> key `missingRecheck` by the requested app (reset on app-identity change), mirroring how PR #4521 fixed the same shape one state over.

**That precedent is in the same file and you should read it first.** Lines ~:268–292 carry the access-probe state that PR #4521 keyed to the app it describes, and its comment at :268 explicitly says *"`missingRecheck` above has the same shape and is deliberately …"*. Mirror the working sibling rather than inventing a second pattern — two different keying styles in one file is how the next reader gets this wrong.

## Zone 2 — the test is the deliverable, not the one-line fix

The fix is small. What makes this card worth an agent is proving it. The reproduction must actually **navigate from one missing app to a second missing app within one mount** and assert a *second* `refreshMetadata` fires. Specifically:

- a test that only mounts with one missing app and asserts one refresh **passes against today's bug** and is worthless;
- red-before / green-after, in that order, on the real defect;
- do not weaken or skip the existing tests around this effect.

Watch the reset direction too: keying by app must not break the existing behaviour that a re-check re-runs when the app *becomes* available again and then goes missing once more. Pin both directions.

## Zone 3 — scope discipline

The card names two neighbours and **both are out of scope**: PR #4521's access-probe state (already fixed and pinned) and **#4486** (MetadataProvider's sessionStorage cache keyed by type, not org — different layer, different cache, still open). If your fix appears to need either, stop and report rather than widening.

Severity context so you calibrate the fix rather than over-engineering: the user cost is one skipped refresh and a not-available screen with a working retry, not a wrong screen. Key the state, pin it, stop.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. Expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the four test shards, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. A clue, not a spec. Changeset required (`@object-ui/app-shell`, patch).

## Premise-first

The card is from 2026-08-13 and the file has moved since (PR #4521 landed in it). I re-measured the target today and it holds, but if the effect has been restructured, follow what you measure — `premise_still_valid: false` with evidence is a legitimate delivery.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #4522`. Push the branch early. Report as JSON and as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5193 (`repo:objectui` seat PM, session `session_01AMHbqfPiETJHA95r6WzZWS`, reviewer of record).

## The instruction was "mirror the sibling" — and it was right not to mirror it blindly

I told you to copy PR #4521's keying rather than invent a second pattern in one file. The state shape does mirror it (`{ app, phase } | null`, read back only for the current app, exactly like `accessProbe`'s `{ app, verdict } | null`). But you diverged on **how the run settles**, and documented why at the call site:

> Settled BY NAME rather than by the `cancelled` flag the probe below uses: this effect re-runs on its own state change, so a cleanup-based cancel would fire on the way out of 'checking' and strand the check there forever.

Copying the sibling wholesale would have introduced a hang — the effect depends on `missingRecheck`, so its own transition into `'checking'` re-runs it and tears down the cleanup that was meant to guard the in-flight refresh. That is a real difference between the two states, found by reasoning about the actual dependency array rather than by pattern-matching. Diverging with a stated reason, at the divergence, is exactly the right handling of a "mirror it" instruction.

And it is **pinned**, not merely argued: the seventh case lands `alpha`'s refresh late, after the URL has already moved to `gamma`, and asserts it does not settle `gamma`'s check. Without that case the by-name settle would be an unverified claim.

## You also fixed the comment that lied

The sibling's comment said `missingRecheck` "has the same shape and is **deliberately left alone**". That sentence became false the moment this card was filed, and it is exactly the kind of stale in-code claim that sends the next reader the wrong way — this repo has several open cards about precisely that failure mode. Corrected in place to say it had the same shape *and the same defect*, with the issue reference. Nobody asked for that.

## The test is what makes this card worth an agent, and it is right

Every one of the 7 cases drives a **real in-mount router navigation** (`useNavigate`, same `<Route element>`, params change, component instance kept), so the second app genuinely meets the first app's state. Your file header states the trap plainly:

> A case that mounts with a single missing app and asserts one refresh passes against the defect — a fresh mount starts from idle, so the skipped re-check is invisible to it.

That is the exact vacuous-test shape I flagged at dispatch, named and avoided.

The red-before split is clean and legible: **3 failed / 4 passed** — the three defect cases red, the four `MUST NOT CHANGE` cases already green. Keeping proving-pins and non-collateral-pins separate is what makes that number readable at a glance. The headline red is user-visible rather than internal (`Unable to find an element by: [data-testid=console-layout]` at `/apps/beta` — the second app never re-checked), and the ablation's reader is verified: relative import of `../AppContent`, so vitest reads the working tree and no `dist` can launder the result.

Wider gates confirm non-collateral: the full `packages/app-shell` suite at 436 files / 4212 tests green, **including PR #4521's own pin file unchanged and passing** — which is the check that matters most when you touch a file two states share.

## Scope

Three files — changeset, `console/AppContent.tsx`, new test. Exactly the declared region. `views/**` and `hooks/**` untouched, so the parallel claim on #5178 was respected; both named neighbours (PR #4521's probe, and #4486's MetadataProvider cache) left alone as instructed.

## Honest reporting worth naming

The `settle()` helper carries a comment explaining it is deliberately not `act`-wrapped, pointing at **#5194** — and it names `LoadingScreen`'s recurring interval as the obvious suspect and then **explicitly disowns it as the diagnosis**, because two of the three measurements were taken after that component had unmounted. Filing a finding while refusing to guess its cause is better than a confident wrong root cause; the next person gets the measurements without inheriting a false lead.

**Landing:** path surface is `packages/app-shell/src/console/**` + changeset — no governed face, queue-eligible. CI still converging at review time (Lint, Type Check and the four shards in flight). I flip ready and enqueue only on terminal success of every required job, read by name.

**Diagnosis is (b) — the red WAS this change, and my review missed it.** `repo:objectui` seat PM, session `session_01AMHbqfPiETJHA95r6WzZWS`.

Verdict, measured rather than argued: **3/3 green on `origin/main`, 3/3 red on the branch**, bisected to `AppContent.tsx`, **4250 un-acted updates in the first second** and the element still absent after 9s. Not the lazy-import timing race it resembled — an **infinite render loop**.

## What I got wrong, on the record

When I triaged the red I reasoned it through and concluded the change was *behaviourally inert* for a resolved app:

> `setMissingRecheckRun` with a functional updater returning the same value (`null` → `null`) — React bails out, no re-render. Same as before.

That was wrong, and it is wrong in a specific, instructive way. The new code comment names the exact trap I fell into:

> do not "simplify" it into an unconditional `setMissingRecheckRun(null)` (or **the functional form `run => run === null ? run : null`, which reads as if React's bailout covers it**)

`refreshMetadata` is a dep of this effect and its identity comes from the **host's** metadata context. The shipped `MetadataProvider` memoizes it, but a host — or a test mock — handing back a fresh function every render makes the effect run after every render. The original code's `if` guard made that a no-op. Replacing it with an unconditional setState turned a benign re-run into a loop, and what the loop starves is the **lazy route inside `ConsoleLayout`**, which then never mounts.

So the failing test was not a flake, not a slow runner, and not the neighbouring package's problem. It was a real regression that would have blanked a console page, and the only thing standing between it and `main` was a pre-existing test in **another package** that nobody had thought to run.

**This is why the red was not re-run.** My own hypothesis — loaded runner, lazy chunk, `findByTestId`'s 1s default — was plausible, matched the symptom, and was completely wrong. "Flaky, re-run it" would have shipped an infinite render loop.

## On the fix

The guard is restored, the dep array now includes `missingRecheckRun` (needed since the guard reads it), and the reason is written into the code as a ⛔ comment with the measurement attached — so the next person who wants to tidy that `if` away has the number in front of them.

The pin deserves specific credit for what it does **not** do:

> The pin asserts the CONSEQUENCE rather than a render count — this surface already churns under these mocks on unmodified main (20 and 66 renders per 20ms window; the fix lowers it to 2 and 12), so any bound tight enough to catch the loop would also fail on main.

A render-count assertion is the obvious pin here and it would have been flaky by construction. Pinning the observable consequence — a lazy child mounted through `extraRoutes` under a resolved app with an unstable `refresh` identity, red against the looping version, green with the guard — is the correct choice and it was reasoned, not stumbled into.

The branch also merged current `main` (`57e668f13`), so parallel discipline 3 is satisfied and the re-run is against the version this will actually merge into.

## Status

Earlier **ACCEPT** stands on everything it covered — the keying, the by-name settle, the seven-case navigation test — but it plainly did not cover this, and I am recording that rather than quietly folding it in. CI is re-running on the new head: 17 terminal, all success; four shards still in flight. I flip ready and enqueue only on terminal success of every required job, read by name.
